text:
aj: quick check — deploying new sidecar via our umbrella chart but imagePullSecrets aren't being applied to the injected pod. I set imagePullSecrets under top-level values and also under chart-specific `sidecar.imagePullSecrets` but only the main app pod gets the secret. has anyone hit odd precedence here?

aj: here's the minimal values I tried:
```yaml
imagePullSecrets:
  - name: reg-creds-main
sidecar:
  enabled: true
  imagePullSecrets:
    - name: reg-creds-sidecar
```

aj: helm version: 3.9, chart: umbrella that includes `app` and `sidecar` as local charts. helm install used the umbrella values file.

rachel: helm value precedence is: cli --set > -f (specified) > chart defaults. For subcharts you either put values under the subchart key (e.g. `sidecar.imagePullSecrets`) or use `global.imagePullSecrets` if the subchart reads from global. If your sidecar template only references `.Values.imagePullSecrets` in its own chart, top-level `imagePullSecrets` in umbrella won't flow unless the umbrella forwards it into the subchart (or the subchart uses `required`/global).

rachel: quick way to confirm: `helm template ./umbrella -f values.yaml | yq '.spec.template.spec.imagePullSecrets'` — inspect the rendered podSpec for the sidecar. Also `helm get values <release>` after install to see the effective merged values.

laura: another angle: remember `imagePullSecrets` is a podSpec field. If the sidecar is injected by a mutating webhook (sidecar injector), the injector needs to copy imagePullSecrets into the final podSpec, not the subchart template. Are you using a manual sidecar chart or cluster injector?

aj: it's a static sidecar container in the same Deployment manifest (not a webhook). so it's just the pod spec in the `sidecar` subchart. I think the chart author used `.Values.imagePullSecrets` in the subchart, not `.Values.sidecar.imagePullSecrets`.

pradeep: if the subchart expects `.Values.imagePullSecrets` (top-level key), then put it under `global` in umbrella or add an alias in umbrella's values: `sidecar:
  imagePullSecrets: {{ .Values.imagePullSecrets }}` — easier: add `global.imagePullSecrets` and change subchart to check global as fallback:
```gotmpl
{{- if .Values.sidecar.imagePullSecrets }}
  imagePullSecrets: {{ toYaml .Values.sidecar.imagePullSecrets | nindent 8 }}
{{- else if .Values.global.imagePullSecrets }}
  imagePullSecrets: {{ toYaml .Values.global.imagePullSecrets | nindent 8 }}
{{- end }}
```

pradeep: also, serviceAccount.imagePullSecrets is another pattern: if chart creates a ServiceAccount and sets `imagePullSecrets` on it, pods using that SA will inherit credential lookup on admission. But most charts put `imagePullSecrets` directly on the podSpec.

aj: got it — makes sense. two followups: (1) easiest immediate fix is to move secret name under the exact subchart key (i.e. `sidecar.imagePullSecrets`) in umbrella values? (2) long-term, should we standardize charts to read `global.imagePullSecrets` as canonical?

rachel: (1) yes, change umbrella values to set `sidecar.imagePullSecrets` and run `helm template` to verify. (2) standardized `global` is nice for org-wide creds, but watch out for multi-registry cases; global assumes same creds across charts. For private registries per-service, prefer per-chart keys.

laura: also add a lint/CI check: `helm template | yq` assertions that if `sidecar.enabled` then `spec.template.spec.imagePullSecrets` is non-empty when expected. Catches this early.

pradeep: if you want, I can push a tiny patch to the sidecar chart to fallback to `global.imagePullSecrets` and add a note in the chart README.

aj: that'd be great, thanks. i'll try the quick values override first and report back. :thumbsup:

aj: thanks all — will follow up once verified.
